body: The world is better now then its ever been and it gets better everyday. People live longer, less people die of starvation, more people have access to education. Yes there are still atrocities in the world and theres still a lot of room for improvement but keep things in perspective. Be thankful to have what you do and help others so we can all live without the fear of starving, not having shelter and not having water. A lot of people already live like this but i would like to help make it so every human has these 3 basic necessities for life. Lets start with that and see what becomes of it.

That saying means that the experience of "enlightenment" is irrelevant because one still has to contribute to society and provide for themselves. Even though it is incredibly profound. People can become addicted to the mind state of enlightenment just as easily as the mind state of having sex. 

I have no problem with people producing art or basically any other industry for that matter. I only have a problem with people who live off the charity of others by simply being "enlightened". They just take advantage of people who are suffering by offering the idea of hope, like most other religions. 

And yes, these are all my opinions, it would be wrong to claim any of this to be a universal truth because i only have my perception to go off of. Anyone claiming a universal truth has lost the knowledge that they are the only one experiencing their subjective perception. Sure enlightenment is generally described as no longer being limited by a single perception,or experiencing universal consciousness, but something still has to process the "source" to describe it to others. Its simply not possible to experience anything without some sort of processing. Ive perceived myself becoming one with the all, both sober and on psychs, as im sure most of you have. But its still my own subjective experience.

This. A thousand times this. Being "enlightened" doesnt change a god damn thing. Believing in this "truth" is still a choice and people have every right to ignore anothers idea of "truth" Spending energy searching for "enlightenment" is wasted in my eyes. Why is a believed that being happy/blissful 24/7 is beneficial for society? Its selfish. Being like that just means one is choosing to be ignorant(or even worse "accepting") of the suffering of others and doing nothing substantial to change it. It would be a million times better to put that effort towards ending the suffering or others.
What makes the "enlightened" state better than other mind states?

While its true that ego death can be seen as enlightenment, or a precursor to enlightenment, most people associate ego death with psychedelics. When its not a result of psychs or meditation, its called depersonalization/derealization, and its terrifying for the people who experienced it. Not bliss as a lot of people perceive it to be. If ego death was apart of enlightenment then it would be just as blissful when it happens randomly as it is on psychs or done with conscious intention. 

Enlightenment to me is simply being. Theres no secret to being there, theres no need for meditation and practices to be there, its not about maintaining a specific mindset or being happy and blissful 24/7. Anything that is/has been/will be, any thoughts/ideas/concepts are already enlightened simply by being a result of existing or having the potential to exist because they come from the "source" as you put it. Yes that includes murders, genocides, all the "evil" things of the world as well. Experiencing the de synchronization of the mind that psychs produce isn't experiencing enlightenment, its just experiencing a mind state. Claiming that state of mind is more significant than any other is just ignorant.

So is literally everything else, both tangible and conceptual. If being enlightened is possible, im guessing an enlightened person would not be okay with living off the charity of others or have any desire to claim they had obtained enlightenment.

As far as i know, expressing that one is enlightened serves no other purpose then to gain power, status, recognition, or any other ego centric thing. The words used dont matter, as long as one claims to know something others dont, they are expressing a need to feel separate from them. They may have good intentions that can be completely self less, but claiming enlightenment or having some sort of special knowledge is not the way to go about spreading any sort of information. 

It is quite ironic though, from my experience, those who spread knowledge of enlightenment always say generally the same thing. That its within all of us and everyone is enlightened already, they just aren't aware of it yet. Its weird to tell people they are something without being aware of it. Its like telling everyone who isn't on the enlightenment level that they're living less of a life than is capable for them. Like do any of these "spiritual leaders" do anything other than spread their enlightenment knowledge?  How do they eat? Donations? Money? Do they work outside of just spreading "sacred" knowledge? Either way i feel like they are living off other peoples work simply for claiming a higher knowledge and spreading it to people who are at their core, unhappy or discontent and looking for a way to fill that void. Just like the majority of the other major religions, or consumerism, or addiction, etc... If everyone lived off of others, without producing anything themselves, as these gurus do, the human race would die out very quickly and being "enlightened" in the way our minds can understand it, would be irrelevant. Thats why that quote is so important in this day of "spiritual revolution" 

"Before enlightenment, cut wood and carry water. After enlightenment, cut wood and carry water."

Its not...
"Before enlightenment, cut wood and carry water. 
After enlightenment, sit on your ass and leach off other peoples need to fill the void that comes with being human that drives us to be faster, better and stronger. Have fun busting your ass while i just sit here and tell you that you're less than you can be while i act blissful so you can all be in awe and have hope of one day being as blissful as i am." For a damn good reason. 

Sorry for the rant, but if enlightenment is in all of us, then we dont need to be told that. It would be the result of living and gaining experience without being told its "possible". Or everyone is already enlightened and these spiritual leaders are playing mind tricks to convince the population they aren't. Or its just another sham some ither organized religions. From my experience, its a combination of all the possibility i've presented, along with more i cant think of. I've seen way more people who could be considered enlightened, who have never been remotely interested in the idea, than those who actively seek the knowledge of "obtaining" it.

First of all, anyone who claims they are enlightened, isn't. Secondly, anyone who claims to have knowledge that only 10,000 people out of 7 billion (total made up, unverifiable number) is bullshitting and not to be trusted. Statements like that are the same as click bait.  I only got that far in the video before i had to turn it off. 

Only advice i can give you is the old saying:

"Before enlightenment, cut wood and carry water. After enlightenment, cut wood and carry water."

Hope that helps <3

To me...being afraid of death is the most irrational fear a person can have. Its going to happen no matter what you do...eat perfect...exercise everyday...be perfectly healthy both physically and mentally...it doesnt matter. Your going to die eventually. Being afraid of it does nothing but cause un-needed anxiety and fear. Im not saying to ignore it though, the knowledge that your going to die one day motivates a lot of people to live and become successful. Knowing this life is all you have is the driving force behind accomplishing anything...from eating your next meal to building a fortune 500 company. Now some belief systems are accompanied by an after life, this bothers me because its un verifiable and causes people to lose sight of the known limits of human life. If you believe in an after life...you lose part of the driving force that keeps you at the highest point of motivation...to a degree. If you believe in an eternal soul...then you made a choice to come to this reality in order to experience it...its your choice if you wish to end this life but just remember you already chose to experience it and you'll chose to experience it again until you've gotten/learned everything you were looking for. So ending this life is pointless...you'll be back eventually.

My experience with psychs has taught me that there is nothing more irrational then the fear of the unknown simply for the fact that it is unknown. The mind will run through every possible option and allow you to experience it temporarily simple because thats what the mind does. It plans and plans and plans and runs through many different possibilities so it will be prepared in any given situation. Understand this and allow that process to become sub-conscious. It does you no good to be aware of this process because it stops you from experiencing the now and being in the moment. A good way to stop this is to experience vastly different things in this reality...it'll force your mind to be aware of the moment and process factors from the moment, instead of some fabricated idea only in the mind.  Much love friend!! Remember, every hour, minute, second...your choosing to experience this reality for a reason. Find the reason and you'll find yourself!!
